findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC was unable to provide information verifying that the food handler at the time of food preparation what completed the Certified Food Protection Manager course and passed the test. The situation was discussed and they were instructed to have sufficient CFPMs available to cover all food preparation shifts in the facility and to maintain copies of these certification at the facility for verification.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

The PIC during the inspection was unable to provide proof that employee were notified in a verifiable manner their need to provide information related to foodborne illnesses related to themselves. The PIC was instructed to provide this information prior to the scheduled follow up.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code. 

Containers of frozen foods in the walk in freezer were observed open and with ice condensate from the condenser unit inside of the packaging and in contact with the foods. The PIC was shown and discarded the items during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. The PIC was instructed to ensure that all foods are protected from contamination at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) (REPEAT) Multiple nozzles of the fountain drink machines were observed heavily soiled during this inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned all nozzles during this inspection to correct. These items should be cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitized) daily or every other day moving forward. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch at all times in the facility. 2) The blade of the can opener in the kitchen was observed with food debris stuck to it. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean at all times in the facility. The blade was cleaned during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

Single service boats were observed in front of the fryers. They had the food contact surfaces up/exposed. These items need to be stored face down at least so that drips, splash or other contaminates are not a concern for contaminating the food contact surface. The PIC was shown and instructed to store the single service items in such a way as to protect them from contamination moving froward.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The PIC during the inspection was unable to provide test strips for the sanitizer used in the facility. Education was conducted and they were instructed to acquire the test strips prior to the scheduled follow up.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

1) (REPEAT) Major ice and frost accumulation was observed in the walk in freezer. 2) The shelving where the trash cans were stored in the customer areas was observed heavily soiled on the bottoms as well as on the walls and doors. 3) Dust was observed on the fan covers in the walk in cooler sufficient that sections appeared ready to fly off and potentially contaminate foods. The PIC was shown all noted locations and instructed to review cleaning procedures and ensure that cleaning is taking place thoroughly and regularly moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). 

The coving at the floor/wall junction below the fountain drink machines was observed pulling away from the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair/replace the coving prior to the next routine inspection and maintain the physical facility in a state of good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Nozzles of the fountain drink machine are observed soiled during this inspection. The PIC was shown and replaced all nozzles during this inspection with the back ups to correct. Per the PIC the nozzles are cleaned weekly. This should be more often as the needs of the facility require. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

The ambient air thermometer in the prep cooler is observed broken and non-functioning at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and placed another thermometer in the cooler to correct the violation. Ensure that all coolers have a correctly functioning thermometer available in them at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

1) Major ice and frost accumulation is observed in the walk in freezer. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and to clean often enough to maintain the area free of frost and ice. 2) The floor in the walk in cooler has filth accumulation in corners that needs to be clean more thoroughly. The PIC was shown and instructed review cleaning procedures and ensure that cleaning is taking place thoroughly and regularly moving forward.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At the time of this inspection there is not a CFPM on site. Pizzas were observed coming out of the oven and being sliced then displayed. Food handling activities are taking place. Ensure that there is a CFPM available at all times that foods are being handled/prepared. Acquire enough CFPMs prior to the next routine inspection in order to cover all times of food handling/preparation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival there were not any paper towels available for hand washing in the kitchen. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the available dispenser was refilled to correct.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

During this inspection the PIC could not show food handler cards for employees at the facility. One employee is still in their training period and is not being considered at this time but the other two could not show completed food handler training. Food handler certificates are on the networked system for Road Ranger. Ensure that all employees that handle RTE or TCS foods have completed food handler training and that the certificates are available prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cheeses and meats in the open faced end cap cooler are observed with temperatures ranging in the 50s-60s. The PIC removed all of the items from this cooler and is in the process of wasting them. A work order has been placed for repairs on this cooler.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The cooler noted on line item #22 needs repaired so that it can maintain effective cold holding temperatures. Follow up is being set for two weeks for compliance.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine are observed soiled. PIC indicated that weekly cleaning takes place for these items and that it will be changed to bi-weekly after this. The items were replaced with clean ones and the soiled ones moved to dish for cleaning.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

A spray bottle behind the service counter is without a label indicating the chemical stored within. PIC indicated that it was window cleaner and a label was added to the bottle to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival the bottle of sanitizer hooked up to the dispenser in the kitchen was empty. A new bottle was added to the dispenser to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizers are available for use at all times that foods (and food contact) are being handled and prepared.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Two unlabeled spray bottles observed (one in the kitchen, one behind the service counter). CORRECTED- According to PIC, spray bottle in the kitchen contains oven cleaner and was labeled as such. Counter spray bottle contained water and was emptied.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed employee rinse out a reusable cup hand washing sink behind the cash registers. Hand washing sink must be used for handwashing only. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Provided education.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured less than 200 ppm at three compartment sink. CORRECTED- PIC remade sanitizer to correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a minumum concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. (P)

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment: Chlorine bleach sanitizer (spray bottle behind the cash register counter) bleached out inspector's test strips, exceeding the maximum toxic level for use on a food-contact surface, as specified by manufacturer. CORRECTED- PIC explained that bleach is only used to clean bathrooms. Employee labeled bottle as such to prevent accidental misuse.
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions
generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for
use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions). (P)

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment: Prepackaged baked goods are not properly labeled. Label with: 1) common name of food, 2) ingredients, 3) net quantities, 4) name and address of packager, 5) food allergens, 6) nutrition labeling, 7) salmonid fish additives used. CORRECTED- PIC used in-house device to print appropriate labels for baked goods. Sign with labels will be posted near baked goods case. Labels must be available to customers upon request.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11 (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), and (6) of this section. (C)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.153 - Pizzas at front counter had surface temperatures below 120°F. Pizzas, like all other hot foods, are time controlled. They are served or discarded within 4hrs or less. All other products had proper labels showing the 4hr time frame, but pizzas were not labeled. A wax pencil is to be used for tracking the time at the pizza holding station but was not used this morning. Proper labeling of time controlled foods was discussed. Make sure the time is being properly tracked for pizzas along with all other hot foods.

Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold hot food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - The stem and holding case of the digital stem thermometer used for checking food temperatures were soiled with food debris and grease. The thermometer was not properly cleaned and sanitized after the last time it was used, which was likely the evening proper according to staff. The thermometer and case were cleaned/sanitized and calibrated during the inspection.

Food and equipment shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times. Sanitize the food thermometer before and after temperature checks, and properly wash, rinse, and sanitize the thermometer up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - Scoop used for portioning candied nuts at the front counter was observed with the handle stored in the product. Proper storage of scoop was discussed. Scoop was positioned to remove handle from the product.

Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 530 - Kitchen employee picked up a food crumb from parchment paper covering cookies in the kitchen and then placed it in his mouth. Employee was advised to cease the practice of eating while in the food prep/service areas. Employee washed his hands upon request of the inspector.
NOTE: The employee in question was observed using proper technique perfectly and was complimented on the good practice of proper handwashing.

Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Wiping cloths were observed hanging on spray bottles of degreaser and sanitizer in the kitchen. Proper use and storage of wiping cloths were discussed. Cloths in question were placed in soiled linen storage area. 
Use disposable paper towels with spray bottles and discard after single use. If wiping cloths are to be used, then provide a solution in a container that will allow for proper storage of said wiping cloths in sanitizer between uses.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - A hair pick was observed sitting on top of a box of single use gloves at the front counter. Hair pick was discarded at the discretion of the store manager.

Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed whipped cream in a dispenser that stated the shelf life was 5 days at ambient room temperature. There was no date mark observed on the bag. For this item follow the date marking procedure listed on the bag (5 days). Employee discarded whipped cream. Also observed whole milk in a creamer dispenser at 38F with no date marking noted. Employee stated they go through multiple bags a week of the milk. Employee was allowed to date mark the bag. Ensure that ready-to-eat PHFs are date marked with the day they were opened, held at proper temperatures, and discarded after 7 days. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in freezer to have an accumulation of ice on the ceiling and on the floor. Ensure that the ice is either removed, or the freezer defrosted, to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizer solution prepared during inspection while food was being served. Employee stated she was unaware that sanitizer was required during regular service and they had been using windex to clean around the food surfaces in the facility. Employee was educated on proper practice. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is prepared and available during hours of food service/preparation. 
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the inside of the Deli Express microwave to have an accumulation of food debris and napkins. Ensure that food contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized regularly. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the front door to have significant light showing between the doors and the weather stripping to be worn down. Ensure that openings to the outside are protected from the entry of pests. 
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink in the kitchen and the hand sink by the office to have no caulking around the edges. Ensure that the hand sinks are caulked to the wall to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed antifreeze stored on top of a box of Monster Energy Drinks. Employee moved the antifreeze during the inspection. Ensure that chemicals are stored below and away from food and drinks. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
750.110g - Muffins and cookies pre-packaged for sale on-site were observed without proper labeling. Provide proper labeling for individually wrapped back goods that are pre-packaged for sale.

Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name; name, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.250 - An open bottle of Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce was observed with other condiments at the hotdog counter. The label states "Refrigerate After Opening", and the product was observed at 70F. The BBQ sauce was discarded in the trash during the inspection. Manager was advised the sauce must be held cold in a cooler once opened, and if desired, smaller portions may be placed in properly labeled bottles in the condiment area as long as the product is time controlled (use or discard w/in 4hrs). 

Potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41F/below while on display and service.
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - A) Containers of hotdogs and other roller grill items were observed without proper date marks. Cheddarwarst and a product labeled beef tamales did not dates. Another container of hotdogs had a date of what appeared to be 10/10, and the Nathan's hotdogs were labeled 10/6. Based on information provided by staff, the Nathan's and beef tamales were discarded and other items were labeled and kept for use. 

B) Various items were observed to be improperly date marked. Portions of foods (boiled eggs; cheese curds; cantaloupe) had use by dates on packages of 10/25. Manager noted they were portioned on 10/18, which would mean the use by date on the bottom of containers should be 10/24. The same issue was observed with products in the top holding area of the  pizza prep cooler. Pepperoni was labeled with prep and discard dates of 10/18 & 10/25; sausage and ham were labeled with prep dates of 10/13 & 10/17 and discard dates of 10/20 & 10/24 respectively. Proper dating and discard of ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods were discussed with Manager. Dating will be discussed with staff to ensure everyone understands date marking.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous, ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. Day 1 starts the moment the original packaging is opened. For example, items opened and/or portions on 10/13 would have a discard date of 10/19.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Tube of hazelnut creamer in the dispenser was observed to be cut straight across and allowing for product to puddle in the dispensing tube. Cut tubes at an angle to allow  proper drainage of product from tubes between uses.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - A) Manager was observed washing hands without use of proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without use of a barrier. 

B) Employee stocking roller grill put on a glove without first washing hands. Employee was advised hands need to be properly washed prior to putting on gloves for food prep. Employee stated she washed her hands in the back room prior to retrieving the package of tornadoes being placed in the rollers. However, the door handle was touched to exit the kitchen area, and the handle is not a clean surface. Employee and manager were advised the front handsink in the food/drink area needs to be utilized for handwashing prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes and prior to working with food and stocking single service articles.  

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have become contaminated, before putting on gloves, between glove changes, and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. After washing hands for 20 seconds with soap and running water, then use paper towels to properly dry hands. Use the paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating freshly washed hands.
.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - A) Covering on shelf was loose beneath the microwave at the hotdog counter. Repair the covering on the shelf. 

B) Haagen Daz freezer was observed with heavy ice buildup inside. Defrost the ice cream freezer.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
750.820c - Tupperware containers used for storage of foods were observed with old labels. Managers stated it appeared the labels were not being removed prior to ware washing. 

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil. Make sure labels are removed from all storage containers and repeat the ware washing process as many times as necessary to ensure all surfaces are being properly cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Cold water was turned on at the 3 part sink in kitchen and was initially very hot. Maintenance worker noted it takes several minutes sometimes for the cold water to actually get cold at all the sinks in the building. Cold water was turned on at the mopsink in the kitchen and also noted to be hot at first. The water eventually got cold, but it fluctuated between cold and getting a little warm and then back to cold. Manager noted she would place a work order to look into the issue.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the bottom inside of some of the cabinets in the coffee area and the roller cooker area had some spillage and soil.
Clean these areas as necessary.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed that the waste containers in the women's rest room does not have a cover.
Provide a cover for the waste can.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed that the floor in the corner of the kitchen area, under the counter by the mop sink, has some soil.  
Clean the floor in this area.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed two spray bottles of liquids that were not labeled. These bottles contained cleaning solutions.
Label all containers of toxic chemicals. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
CORRECTED = Bottles were labeled as to the contents.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed that the damp mop was stored in the mop bucket in the store room. 
Store the mop hanging upright to promote air drying.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the inside of the 3 door reach in freezer in the store room had some spillage and debris in the bottom of the unit.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Clean this unit.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of single -service items stored on the floor in the store room.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
Store items properly.
CORRECTED= Boxes were placed on storage shelf.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed there is a waste container in  the men's restroom that does not have a lid on the container.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.
Provide cover for the waste receptacle.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed that the floor in the store room and in the walk in cooler had some soil.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.
Clean the floors.
